question: When did humans become food producers in history?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Neolithic Age Middle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Neolithic Age**, also known as the **New Stone Age**, marked a revolutionary transition in human history from **hunting-gathering** to **food production**.
 
• During this period, humans began practicing **agriculture**, domesticating animals, and settling in permanent communities.
 
• The shift to food production occurred around **10,000 BCE** in some parts of the world, particularly in regions like the **Fertile Crescent** in the Middle East.
 
• Tools became more advanced, with the development of **polished stone tools** used for farming and other daily activities.
 
• Pottery was invented to store food and water, which was essential for settled agricultural life.
 
• Humans began cultivating staple crops such as **wheat, barley, rice, and millet**, depending on the geographical region.
 
• This age witnessed the rise of small villages and the beginning of a more organized social structure.
 
• The Neolithic Revolution laid the foundation for the development of **civilizations**, leading to advancements in technology, art, and governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Stone Age**__

 __
 
• The Stone Age is divided into three periods: **Paleolithic, Mesolithic, and Neolithic**.
 
• During the **Paleolithic Age**, humans were primarily hunter-gatherers and used **basic stone tools**.
 
• The **Mesolithic Age** introduced more advanced tools and some early signs of food cultivation.
 
• However, large-scale food production was not characteristic of the Stone Age until the **Neolithic period**.
 
 
 
• **Paleolithic Age**__
 __
 
• The **Paleolithic Age**, or the Old Stone Age, primarily involved a lifestyle of **hunting and gathering**.
 
• Humans used rudimentary tools made of stone, wood, and bone.
 
• There was no evidence of organized agriculture or food production during this period.
 
• Humans were nomadic and depended on natural resources for survival.
 
 
 
• **Copper Age**__
 
 
• The **Copper Age**, also known as the **Chalcolithic Age**, marked the transition from the Stone Age to the Bronze Age.
 
• It was characterized by the use of **copper tools and weapons** but did not see significant advancements in food production.
 
• Humans continued agricultural practices initiated during the Neolithic Age.
 
• This age is often associated with the rise of early civilizations and more complex social structures.
